messages.content:
You are synthesizing a restricted supervisory program for a simulated factory corridor shared by two autonomous mobile robots, A and B, with a pedestrian crossing. Use only this message. Do not use tools, read files, browse, or consult other attempts. Produce exactly one UTF-8 JSON object as the complete response, without Markdown fences, explanatory prose, comments, or additional fields. This is a bounded formal specification task, not unrestricted robotic planning.

The root has exactly three keys: "schema", "select", "step". The schema value is "amr-supervisor/v1". Both functions are arrays of ordered rules, with at most eight rules in each function. A select rule has exactly "when" (expression string) and "action" (string). A step rule also requires "next" (mode string). At most 32 total branches are allowed; the per-function limit of eight still applies. Source size is at most 200 * 1024 bytes.

The first rule whose expression evaluates to true determines the result. Every possible input must have a result. Expressions allow only True, False, the permitted Boolean names, not, and, or, and parentheses, with Python Boolean precedence. No calls, comparisons, arithmetic, attributes, new names, or assignment. A condition has at most 512 characters, 64 Python syntax-tree nodes and expression depth eight. Duplicate JSON keys are rejected.

select inputs: OwnerFree, RequestA, RequestB, PreferA, PreferB. Its possible actions are SelectA, SelectB, Defer. OwnerFree states that the shared corridor reservation is available. RequestA/RequestB indicate requests. PreferA/PreferB are advisory. Selecting A requires OwnerFree and RequestA; selecting B requires OwnerFree and RequestB. If a reservation is free and at least one request exists, select an eligible robot, rather than Defer. Otherwise Defer is required. When both robots are eligible, either is legal; preferences do not impose an additional acceptance obligation, and their values may conflict or both be absent.

step inputs: ObservationUsable, PedestrianBlocked, OwnReservation, Released, BodyClearOfZ, Halted, AtGoal, TaskActive. ObservationUsable means the observation has passed the trusted freshness/identity checks. PedestrianBlocked denotes a blocked crossing. OwnReservation denotes this robot's ownership. Released denotes an acknowledged reservation release for its task; it is distinct from BodyClearOfZ, which states that the whole body is clear of the controlled zone. Halted is a trusted stop confirmation, not merely the issuance of a Brake command. AtGoal and TaskActive have their literal task meanings. The generated program cannot alter these facts.

Current mode is exactly one of Idle, Waiting, Traversing, BrakeRequested, Stopped, ResumePending, Done. A step expression may also refer to ModeIdle, ModeWaiting, ModeTraversing, ModeBrakeRequested, ModeStopped, ModeResumePending, ModeDone. Exactly one such mode flag is true. select cannot use any step or mode names; step cannot use any select names.

step actions: Request, Proceed, Brake, Resume, Release, Finish. Each rule returns its action and explicit next mode. Mode names are the same seven names above, without a Mode prefix in the "next" value. No special terminal-mode shortcut exists: the requirements apply in every mode, including Done. All 32 combinations of select facts and all 7 * 256 combinations of mode and step facts are evaluated, even combinations not physically reachable. Do not infer relationships between Boolean inputs beyond the one-hot mode flags.

The following policy section gives required behavior and priority. Synthesize expressions and order them to satisfy that policy within the eight-rule function limit. The evaluation will use the unchanged policy, an independent model interpreter and source/model correspondence checking. No reference controller or example solution is supplied.

Policy presentation P3: dispatcher's decision procedure.

At every update the dispatcher first asks whether the observation can be used, the task remains active, and the crossing is free of a pedestrian block. If any of these three checks fails, its instruction is Brake. Stop confirmation then decides the next mode: Halted means Stopped, and no Halted means BrakeRequested. No other instruction takes precedence over this instruction.

Only when all three checks succeed does the dispatcher consider a released robot at its goal. AtGoal together with Released requires Brake/BrakeRequested until Halted, and then Finish/Done. For inputs not handled so far, a robot that owns the reservation and has its entire body clear of the zone must report Release/Traversing. Clear body and released reservation are separate facts.

For the remaining inputs, first retain Brake/BrakeRequested if the current mode is BrakeRequested and stop confirmation is still absent. If this does not apply, require Request/Waiting when ownership and released status are both absent. If that also does not apply, a Stopped robot takes Resume/ResumePending. Every input left over takes Proceed/Traversing.

Each slash above separates the returned action from the exact next mode. The order of these checks is normative, including for inconsistent-looking Boolean facts and current Done mode. Reservation selection has precisely the constraints given in the interface; no extra preference-following requirement is added. Return just the complete program JSON.
